headline: Indonesian Traffic Police Confirm Driving Licenses Remain Five-Year
seoTitle: Indonesian Traffic Police Deny Lifetime Driving Licenses
metaDescription: Indonesian police clarify that driving licenses must be renewed every five years, dismissing online claims suggesting they are valid for a lifetime.
aiSummaryBullets: Traffic police authorities in Indonesia have formally refuted circulating claims that driving licenses could be valid for a lifetime.
Current national traffic regulations mandate that driving license holders must undergo renewal processes every five years.
Officials cited health and safety assessments as primary reasons for maintaining the five-year validity period instead of a permanent license.
aiContextParagraph: The Indonesian Traffic Police, known as Korlantas, have issued official statements to clarify public misinformation regarding the validity period of national driving licenses. Following viral social media rumors suggesting that licenses might be granted for a lifetime or issued at no cost, authorities reaffirmed that current legal frameworks under the Traffic and Road Transportation Law require regular renewals. Official explanations indicate that the five-year validation cycle is necessary to ensure that drivers maintain the physical and psychological health standards required to operate vehicles safely on public roads. The police have categorized previous online reports regarding permanent status as hoaxes and continue to emphasize that all drivers must adhere to established renewal procedures to remain compliant with national traffic safety standards and operational requirements for road users across the country.
whyItIsViral: The topic is experiencing high public search interest and has been covered by four independent media outlets, driven by the persistent circulation of misinformation regarding government documentation.
